title: Ready to Assign ignores uncategorized credit-card spending, overstating assignable money until month rollover
description:
zeroSum.ts buildLedgers (~line 106) sends uncategorized spending to RTA only on cash accounts: 'if (!card) ledger.uncategorized += net; // R4; R5 on cards: no effect'. A credit-card leg whose category is null or missing (soft-deleted category) therefore funds no payment envelope and does not reduce RTA; the negative payment envelope is only swept out of RTA by nextSweep at the next month rollover. In-month RTA is thus inflated by exactly the unfunded card amount.

Live evidence (budget Casa, 2026-11): cash 60.596,73 = envelopes 0 + RTA 76.070,88 + payment envelopes -15.474,15. Deleting the category 'Saude' while it held the R$ 6.500,00 Itau installment 'CCT CLINICA CIR 01/04' moved RTA 69.570,88 -> 76.070,88 (+6.500,00) and the Itau payment envelope -5.350,84 -> -11.850,84, with no new money. Restoring the category row in memory returns RTA to exactly 69.570,88. December RTA is 60.596,73 = cash, because the sweep absorbs the deficit.

Related: budget_categories_delete soft-deletes with no guard/relink, so deletions orphan live transactions and assignments; assignments of a deleted category silently leave assignedTotal, and orphan cash rows fall into RTA.

Desired: an unbudgeted card spend should reduce RTA in the same month (like the cash case) or be surfaced as a same-month adjustment, so Ready to Assign never exceeds cash minus obligations. Add a regression test at the engine level (uncategorized card spend, and a card leg pointing at a deleted category).
acceptance_criteria: Engine test: a credit-card transaction with category_id null (and one pointing at a deleted category) reduces that month's readyToAssign by its amount, matching the cash-account behavior; a live budget with only that spend keeps cash = envelopes + RTA + payment envelopes with RTA <= cash.
